title: Planner: sprints and backlogs in unified plans
summary: The roadmap facts and both documented licensing controls check out. The cost rationale overstates the licence requirement: Microsoft explicitly gives Microsoft 365 users view-only access to other premium capabilities, so not everyone who wants access to sprints needs a paid Planner subscription. The claim that most teams already use unified plans is also unsubstantiated.

claims.claim: Licences can be assigned in Microsoft 365 admin center through Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. ... Select the row of the user ... select Licenses and Apps. ... Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: The self-service control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > Self-service trials and purchases > product > Do not allow.
claims.quote: Settings > Org settings ... On the Services tab ... select Self-service trials and purchases. ... select the product name. ... select Allow, Allow for trials only, or Do not allow.

claims.claim: Update-MSCommerceProductPolicy -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase -ProductId CFQ7TTC0HDB1 -Value "Disabled" disables Planner Plan 1 self-service purchases and trials.
claims.quote: Planner Plan 1* | CFQ7TTC0HDB1 | Yes; Disabled | Users can't make self-service purchases or acquire trials for the product. Update-MSCommerceProductPolicy -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase -ProductId <ProductID> -Value "Disabled"
